questionText:
Arrange the following events in Indian politics in chronological order.
(A) The Socialist Party was formed
(B) The Communist Party of India (CPI) abandoned the path of violent revolution
(C) The Swatantra Party was formed
(D) Formation of National Revolutionary Party in Mexico

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
NCERT Class 12 Politics in India Since Independence (Chapter 2: Era of One-Party Dominance): (D) National Revolutionary Party (later PRI) of Mexico was founded in 1929 by Plutarco Elias Calles (p. 39 box). (A) The Congress Socialist Party leaders formed the separate Socialist Party in 1948 after Congress amended its constitution (p. 34). (B) The Communist Party of India (CPI) abandoned the path of violent revolution to participate in general elections in 1951 (p. 35). (C) Swatantra Party was formed in August 1959 under the leadership of C. Rajagopalachari (p. 40). Chronological order: (D) [1929] -> (A) [1948] -> (B) [1951] -> (C) [1959].
Hence, option (C) is correct.

questionText:
Which one of the following statements is not correct about the cultural
consequences of globalisation?

options.text:
The cultural effect of globalization leads to the fear that this process
poses a threat to cultures in the world.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: The rise of a uniform culture is not emergence of a global culture.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text:
The consequences of globalization is strictly confined to the sphere of
politics and economy.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text:
What we have in the name of global culture is the imposition of Western
culture on the rest of the world.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Cultural globalisation impacts food, attire, values, and music worldwide. Far from being confined to politics and economics, globalization exerts powerful cultural effects, creating both cultural homogenisation (spread of Western monoculture) and cultural heterogenisation (appropriation into local contexts). Thus, statement (C) is factually false.
Hence, option (C) is correct.
